definition: to increase suddenly and by a large amount
exampleIELTS: Online sales surged from 12% in 2010 to 38% in 2020, overtaking in-store purchases.

definition: to fall or drop straight down at high speed
exampleIELTS: Coal consumption plummeted from 60 million tonnes to barely 15 million over the period shown.

definition: to rise quickly to a high level
exampleIELTS: The number of international tourists soared, reaching a peak of 2.1 million in 2018.

definition: to stop rising or falling and remain at a steady level
exampleIELTS: After a sharp rise in the first decade, female participation plateaued at around 65%.

definition: to change frequently in size, amount, or quality
exampleIELTS: Unemployment fluctuated between 4% and 7% throughout the period, with no clear upward or downward trend.

definition: to become steady and stop changing
exampleIELTS: Carbon emissions stabilised at approximately 30 megatonnes from 2015 onwards.

definition: to reach the highest level before falling
exampleIELTS: Energy consumption peaked at 850 terawatt-hours in 2008 before declining steadily thereafter.

definition: a small, temporary fall in a level or amount
exampleIELTS: Despite a brief dip in 2015, overall production rose throughout the period.

definition: to rise gradually over time
exampleIELTS: Tuition fees climbed steadily from £3,000 in 2005 to over £9,000 by 2020.

definition: to gradually become smaller or weaker
exampleIELTS: Newspaper readership dwindled over the two decades, falling from 75% to under 30%.

definition: to a large extent or degree
exampleIELTS: The proportion of households owning a smartphone rose substantially, from 23% to 91% over the period.

definition: by a very small amount
exampleIELTS: Public transport usage rose only marginally, by about two percentage points across the decade.

definition: as judged in comparison with something else
exampleIELTS: Spending on healthcare was comparatively high, almost double that of any other category.

definition: in a way that corresponds in size or amount to something else
exampleIELTS: Although Japan's population is smaller, it consumed proportionally more energy per capita than India.

definition: by a sudden and very large amount
exampleIELTS: Renewable energy use increased dramatically, more than tripling between 2000 and 2020.

definition: at a regular and constant rate
exampleIELTS: Car ownership rose steadily across the period, gaining around two percentage points each year.

definition: suddenly and unexpectedly
exampleIELTS: The downward trend ended abruptly in 2018, when figures recovered to pre-recession levels.

definition: the lowest point in a fluctuating series of values
exampleIELTS: Sales reached a trough of just 4,000 units in 2012 before recovering throughout the rest of the decade.

definition: a part or share of a whole
exampleIELTS: A growing proportion of commuters chose cycling over driving during the period shown.

definition: a noticeable difference between two things that should match
exampleIELTS: There is a marked discrepancy between male and female enrolment in engineering, with men outnumbering women three to one.

definition: the overall pattern or path of change over time
exampleIELTS: The two countries followed a similar trajectory, with both seeing rapid urban growth after 2005.

definition: of considerable importance, size, or worth
exampleIELTS: The chart shows a substantial increase in renewable energy use between 2010 and 2020.

definition: so small or unimportant that it can be ignored
exampleIELTS: The change in coal use was negligible, varying by less than one percent across the entire period.

definition: easy to see or recognise
exampleIELTS: There was a noticeable shift towards online shopping, particularly among younger consumers.

definition: following one after another in unbroken sequence
exampleIELTS: Emissions fell for three consecutive years before rising again in the final period.
